s0101.literal: His grandfather Rui was a Liang Opener of the Mansion Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes and Duke Yan of Yongchang.
s0101.idiomatic: His grandfather Rui had been a Liang opener of the mansion equal in honor to the three dukes and Duke Yan of Yongchang.

s0102.literal: His father Zheng, [10] a Liang Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
s0102.idiomatic: His father Zheng [10] had been a Liang attendant of the yellow gate.

s0103.literal: Zai from youth was clever and keen, with a steadfast will and love of learning.
s0103.idiomatic: As a boy Zai was bright and eager, devoted to study.

s0104.literal: At age twelve, following his uncle Ling he saw Liu Xian of Pei; Xian asked ten matters from the Book of Han, and Zai answered each question as it came, never hesitating or stumbling.
s0104.idiomatic: At twelve he went with his uncle Ling to see Liu Xian of Pei. Xian quizzed him on ten points from the Book of Han; Zai answered on the spot without a pause.

s0105.literal: When grown, he ranged widely through letters and histories, was deep and keen, and had capacity and judgment.
s0105.idiomatic: Grown up, he was widely read in letters and history, thoughtful and quick, with real judgment.

s0106.literal: He first entered office as a Liang legal aide to the Prince of Shaoling, was transferred to Crown Prince Attendant and Gentleman of the Three Dukes in the Masters of Writing.
s0106.idiomatic: He began as legal aide to the prince of Shaoling under Liang, then became crown prince attendant and gentleman of the three dukes in the masters of writing.

s0107.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan of Liang, assuming the provisional regime, made him Attendant of the Secretariat.
s0107.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Yuan of Liang, ruling provisionally, made him attendant of the secretariat.

s0108.literal: Soon he became General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Xunyang, following the area commander Wang Sengbian east to attack Hou Jing.
s0108.idiomatic: He was soon made general who establishes might and administrator of Xunyang, marching east under Wang Sengbian against Hou Jing.

s0109.literal: At that time Sengbian's army was at Pencheng, while Lu Sidada, Fan Jun, and others each held troops guarding their borders, watching the outcome.
s0109.idiomatic: Sengbian then lay at Pencheng; Lu Sidada, Fan Jun, and others each held their districts with troops and waited to see who would win.

s0110.literal: Emperor Yuan made Zai Acting with Staff, Area Commander over Military Affairs in the three commanderies of Taiyuan, Gaotang, and Xincai, and Administrator of Gaotang.
s0110.idiomatic: Yuan made Zai acting commander with staff over Taiyuan, Gaotang, and Xincai and administrator of Gaotang.

s0111.literal: He still bore orders to persuade Sidada and the others to take the field and attack Jing.
s0111.idiomatic: He was also charged to win Sidada and the rest over and bring them out against Hou Jing.

s0112.literal: When the great army marched east, Zai led the troops of the three commanderies out from Jiao Lake through Shankou and joined Sengbian at Mount Liang.
s0112.idiomatic: When the main force moved east, Zai led the three commanderies' men from Jiao Lake through Shankou to meet Sengbian at Mount Liang.

s0113.literal: When Jing was pacified, he was made General Who Champions and Administrator of Langye.
s0113.idiomatic: After Hou Jing fell he was made champion general and administrator of Langye.

s0114.literal: Soon he was sent on mission to Dongyang and Jin'an to win over and pacify Liu Yi, Chen Baoying, and others.
s0114.idiomatic: He was soon sent to Dongyang and Jin'an to bring Liu Yi, Chen Baoying, and others over.

s0115.literal: He was then made Trustworthy Martial General and Administrator of Yixing.
s0115.idiomatic: He was then made trustworthy-martial general and administrator of Yixing.

s0116.literal: The Founder executed Wang Sengbian and then sent Zhou Wenyü with light troops to strike Zai; before they arrived Zai had already sensed it and walled the city to hold out.
s0116.idiomatic: After the Founder killed Wang Sengbian he sent Zhou Wenyü with light troops against Zai. Zai saw it coming first and shut the city to resist.

s0117.literal: Wenyü pressed the attack fiercely; the district soldiers under Zai were all the Founder's old troops and many were skilled with crossbows. Zai gathered several dozen men, bound them with long chains, had those he trusted supervise them, and made them shoot at Wenyü's army, stipulating that any who failed to hit twice in ten shots would die; every shot struck, and all who were hit fell dead.
s0117.idiomatic: Wenyü attacked hard. Zai's county levies were many of the Founder's old soldiers and crack crossbowmen. He took several dozen, chained them in a row, set trusted men over them, and made them shoot at Wenyü's host on pain of death if they missed twice in ten tries. Every bolt found its mark and every man hit went down.

s0118.literal: Wenyü's army gradually fell back; he therefore took the water outside the city and set up a palisade, and they faced each other for several tens of days.
s0118.idiomatic: Wenyü's men gave ground. He threw up a river palisade outside the walls, and the two sides stood off for weeks.

s0119.literal: The Founder heard that Wenyü's army was faring ill and then personally led a campaign against him, storming the water palisade.
s0119.idiomatic: Hearing Wenyü was losing, the Founder came in person, stormed the river camp, and broke it.

s0120.literal: He then sent Zai's clansman Hui bearing a letter to explain to Zai the reason for executing Wang Sengbian, and also presented an edict of Emperor Jing of Liang, [edict] ordering Zai to disarm.
s0120.idiomatic: He then sent Zai's cousin Hui with a letter explaining why Wang Sengbian had been killed and with an edict from Emperor Jing of Liang ordering Zai to lay down arms.

s0121.literal: [11] When Zai received the letter, he thereupon led his troops in surrender to the Founder.
s0121.idiomatic: [11] Zai opened the letter and surrendered with his force to the Founder.

s0122.literal: The Founder greatly comforted and reassured him, immediately put his clansman Hui in charge of Yixing commandery, assigned all the generals and officers under him according to their talents, and kept Zai always at his side to consult with him.
s0122.idiomatic: The Founder treated him generously, set his cousin Hui over Yixing, placed his officers each where he could best use them, and kept Zai at his side for counsel.

s0123.literal: Xu Sihui, Ren Yue, and others brought Qi troops across the river and held Stone City; the Founder asked Zai for a plan, and Zai said: "If the Qi army divides its forces and first seizes the roads of the Three Wu, overrunning the eastern borderlands, then the times are lost.
s0123.idiomatic: Xu Sihui and Ren Yue brought Qi troops across the Yangzi and held Stone City. The Founder asked Zai's advice. Zai said, "If Qi splits its army and first takes the routes through the Three Wu and raids the east, the cause is lost.

s0124.literal: Now we should quickly build a city on the Huai at Hou Jing's old rampart to open the eastern supply route, and separately order light troops to cut their grain transport, so that advancing they have nothing to seize and retreating they have nothing to rely on—then the heads of the Qi generals can be had within ten days."
s0124.idiomatic: We should hurry to build a fort on the Huai at Hou Jing's old site to keep the eastern line open, and send light troops to cut their supplies so they cannot feed an advance or a retreat. Then the Qi commanders' heads will be ours within ten days."

s0126.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he left office because of illness.
s0126.idiomatic: In Tianjia year one he resigned on grounds of illness.

s0127.literal: Zai had fields of more than ten qing at White Mountain in Jiangcheng county; at this he built a dwelling and lived there, cutting himself off from human affairs; for joys and sorrows, congratulations and condolences, he went nowhere and for nearly ten years did not pass his hedge gate.
s0127.idiomatic: He owned more than ten qing of land at White Mountain in Jiangcheng and now built a house there, shut out the world, and for nearly ten years never crossed his gate for feast or funeral.

s0128.literal: In the Taijian era he died at home, aged fifty-eight.
s0128.idiomatic: He died at home in the Taijian era, aged fifty-eight.

s0130.literal: His son Hong, courtesy name Deli, had literary talent and rose in office to Aide to the Prince of Yongjia.
s0130.idiomatic: His son Hong, styled Deli, was a man of letters and rose to aide in the household of the prince of Yongjia.

s0131.literal: When Chen perished he entered Sui.
s0131.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered Sui service.

s0132.literal: The historian says: In old times Deng Yu rose from literary study and Du Yu came out of refined Confucian learning, yet in the end they achieved military merit and their fame stands in former ages.
s0132.idiomatic: The historian writes: Deng Yu began in the classics and Du Yu in pure scholarship, yet both won fame in war and live in the histories of old.

s0133.literal: When the Jin house fell into disorder and was driven east across the river, men such as Gu Rong and Xi Jian, and the likes of Wen Jiao and Xie Xuan, were all plain-clothed scholars of gentry repute who resisted the enemy to guard the altars of state and by merit rose to the highest offices.
s0133.idiomatic: When Jin collapsed and fled to the south, Gu Rong and Xi Jian, Wen Jiao and Xie Xuan, were scholar-gentry in plain dress who took up arms for the realm and by merit reached the highest posts.

s0134.literal: From that time down, each age has had such men.
s0134.idiomatic: Since then every age has produced men of that kind.

s0135.literal: Yet when the Liang house seethed, cowards found resolve; having themselves met the moment and being trusted by the rulers of the day—how fine!
s0135.idiomatic: When Liang boiled with war even timid men found their nerve; they met their hour and were armed by their lords—worthy of praise indeed.

s0137.literal: When the fu was finished he presented it; the emperor was pleased and replied by hand—comment: the Northern Supervisory, Ji, Palace, and Hall editions and the attached biography of Shen Zhong in the History of the Southern Dynasties all read "when the fu was finished he presented it; the emperor replied by hand, saying."
s0137.idiomatic: On "when the fu was finished he presented it; the emperor was pleased and replied by hand": Northern Supervisory, Ji, Palace, and Hall editions and Shen Zhong's biography in the Southern Dynasties history read "presented it; the emperor replied by hand, saying."

s0138.literal: When Jing besieged the Terrace City—the two characters "besieged the Terrace" were originally effaced in the base text and are now supplied from the various editions.
s0138.idiomatic: On "when Jing besieged the Terrace City": wei tai was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.

s0139.literal: The court gentlemen together mocked his conduct—the character "gentlemen" was originally effaced in the base text and is now supplied from the various editions.
s0139.idiomatic: On "the court gentlemen together mocked his conduct": shi was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.

s0140.literal: When Zhuang usurped the throne—the character "usurped" was originally effaced in the base text and is now supplied from the various editions.
s0140.idiomatic: On "when Zhuang usurped the throne": jian was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.

s0141.literal: Made Mi Attendant-in-Ordinary and Chief Clerk of the Chancellor—the character "chancellor" was originally effaced in the base text and is now supplied from the various editions.
s0141.idiomatic: On "made Mi attendant-in-ordinary and chief clerk of the chancellor": cheng was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.

s0142.literal: Lin's army was defeated—the two characters "army defeated" were originally effaced in the base text and are now supplied from the various editions.
s0142.idiomatic: On "Lin's army was defeated": jun bai was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.

s0143.literal: On his deathbed he admonished his son Manhua, saying—"Manhua" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Fanghua."
s0143.idiomatic: On "on his deathbed he admonished his son Manhua": the Southern Dynasties history reads Fanghua.

s0146.literal: [Juan]—changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties; the same below.
s0146.idiomatic: [Juan]—emended per the Southern Dynasties history; the same below.

s0147.literal: Comment: Zhang Juan has biographies in both the Book of Liang and the History of the Southern Dynasties.
s0147.idiomatic: Zhang Juan has biographies in the Book of Liang and the Southern Dynasties history.

s0150.literal: also has the phrase "Zhang Juan of Fanyang."
s0150.idiomatic: also has the phrase "Zhang Juan of Fanyang."

s0151.literal: Captured Yu Xiaopin, Li Xiaoqin, and others—comment: above "captured" the two characters "Zhou Di" should be supplied; only then is the sense complete.
s0151.idiomatic: On "captured Yu Xiaopin and Li Xiaoqin": the name Zhou Di is missing before "captured" and should be supplied.

s0152.literal: Father Zheng—the graph zheng (govern) in the Book of Liang and the History of the Southern Dynasties
s0152.idiomatic: On "father Zheng": the Book of Liang and the History of the Southern Dynasties read the graph zheng (govern).

s0155.literal: [edict] ordering Zai to disarm—supplied according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Palace editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties.
s0155.idiomatic: On "[edict] ordering Zai to disarm": supplied from Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Palace editions and the Southern Dynasties history.
